newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia blasts rock opposition protest, kill seven.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia blasts rock opposition protest, kill seven.

text.p: Seven people were killed and 25 injured, 19 of them seriously, in a bomb and grenade attack on an opposition demonstration in the Cambodian capital on Sunday, police said.
Unidentifed attackers threw two grenades from a car that sped up to the demonstration outside the Cambodian National Assembly in Phnom Penh, police and witnesses said.

A bomb also appeared to have exploded in a nearby food vendor's cart as protesters from opposition leader Sam Rainsy's Khmer Nation Party (KNP) demonstrated against what they called subservience of the judiciary to the ruling Cambodian People's Party (CPP).
The protest had been authorised by Phnom Penh municipal authorities.
Rainsy, long a thorn in the side of the government, was nearby when the explosions went off. He was whisked away by aides and his wife Tioulong Saumura told Reuters he was safe.
Many of the dead and injured had been near the food vendor's cart. Blood and placards littered the ground and heavily armed police sealed off the area and the road that leads past the royal palace.
Rainsy was ousted as finance minister in 1994 and formed the KNP in November 1995.
He has since allied the officially unrecognised KNP with the royalist FUNCINPEC party, party of an uneasy coalition with the CPP, to fight elections planned for 1998.
